(1) WIDGET-FREEZE (native v61): the home-screen widget froze mid-session two days running (Oct 29 PM stuck 00:58:28 / 34.2 km / 2 loads; Oct 30 stuck again) while the app counted on. Root: TrackerWidget's repaint chain armed every shot with setAndAllowWhileIdle — the INEXACT alarm tier Doze defers; one deferred shot stalled the self-re-arming chain. Fix: the chain now rides DayScheduler.scheduleChainAlarm — the same EXACT tier (setExactAndAllowWhileIdle, manifest grants already declared) the production day alarm uses; inexact only as last resort; alarm-clock tier deliberately unused. Cadence unchanged. Named residual: widget MILES still derive only from web-pushed strings (the native record carries no miles; a second native derivation was rejected) — status/clock/loads now re-derive from the record on time every minute. (2) PIP-HOME / SIS (web): v60 verdict FAILED with video Oct 30 07:40 — Back from navigation on a pre-session drive (dashboard 'Ready to work', no session running) landed on a plain dashboard, no float. Root: the v227 park floats the TRACKER face, which the shell raises only while a session is live; with no session the drive screen parked hidden in the dock and nothing could float. Fix: parkDrive splits on the session — WITH a session the v227 law is untouched (face floats, drive survives hidden); WITHOUT one the drive screen itself floats as the compact mini map (.nv-mini + .nv-pip posture: map visible, compact, mic off the face via mt-pip, map never buried by text), a tap reopens the Navigator full-screen, and the tracker face stands down while a mini is parked (one float at a time — parkedMini() seam). A drive ending under a mini park stands the float down with it. (3) TIMER-DISPLAY-FROZEN (web, the shared root's third surface): the dashboard hero read ~3 s of progress in ~3 min while the session counted (screen showing 'Screen not held — the app may sleep'). The hero's value was always timestamp-true; its only repaint driver, a 1 s setInterval, is the continuation the OS freezes. Fix: App.heroPaint (HERO-PAINT block) — requestAnimationFrame-driven trackerTick on a bounded 200 ms cadence while the dashboard is visible and a session is live, plus an immediate kick on visibilitychange/pageshow/focus so the first glance back paints the true time; the interval stays for the deep-background case.
